title: Verifier‑Assisted versus LLM‑Only Pre‑deployment Network‑Change Validation: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We evaluate whether adding a deterministic pre‑deployment verifier plus a bounded automated repair budget improves the fraction of intent‑driven network‑change proposals that pass semantic validation versus accepting a single LLM candidate. In a preregistered paired design (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) we executed 300 paired intents (100 per difficulty stratum: low/medium/high) using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic semantic validator. Each pair reused the same single shared_initial LLM candidate for two conditions: baseline (accept single shot) and guarded (validator + ≤1 automated repair). Results: baseline 299/300 unflagged passes (0.996667), guarded 300/300 (1.0); contingency n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; absolute paired difference = 0.0033333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.01] (bootstrap_seed = 1729, B = 10000). Provider audit shows 301 model calls (300 shared_initial + 1 repair). Under this synthetic suite and the constrained repair operator, baseline single‑shot generation was near ceiling, producing minimal observable deterministic rescue. We release archived preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts and interpret implications for estimand conditioning, validator coverage, repair budget, and NetOps deployment policies.

sections.introduction:
Automating NetOps tasks with generative LLMs (intent→configuration, template synthesis, automated repair) promises operational efficiency but raises critical semantic‑correctness concerns: sequencing constraints, reachability, and policy preservation are not assured by syntactic fluency. Common engineering patterns pair generative models with deterministic validators and bounded repair (generate→validate→repair) to reduce risk, but reported benefits conflate deterministically rescuing a single generated candidate with benefits from resampling or interactive regeneration. We designed a preregistered paired experiment to isolate the deterministic rescue that a validator plus a bounded repair budget can provide when the same single LLM output is re‑used across conditions. Our primary research question: Does adding a deterministic verifier and at most one automated repair increase the probability that a single LLM candidate passes semantic pre‑deployment validation compared with accepting that same candidate without repair?

Contributions. (1) A preregistered paired evaluation (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) that conditions on a single LLM draw per intent (shared_initial) and measures deterministic rescue under a bounded repair budget. (2) A complete, archived execution and analysis bundle (task manifests, validator traces, repair transcript, inferential artifacts) that supports forensic inspection. (3) An evidence‑grounded interpretation of estimand conditioning, ceiling effects, validator coverage, and operational implications for NetOps CI/CD policies.
sections.related_work: Recent surveys and system papers document rapid advances in LLM applications to NetOps tasks (intent translation, configuration generation, protocol test generation, and repair) and call out the need for semantic evaluation beyond syntactic correctness [1–6]. Several works propose tool‑augmented architectures (planner‑centric frameworks, ReAct‑style agents) enabling LLMs to call external validators, simulators, or synthesizers to coordinate multi‑step workflows [7,8]. Empirical reports indicate that deterministic checks and generate→validate→repair scaffolds can improve correctness metrics relative to unconstrained generation, but gains depend strongly on validator expressiveness, task distribution, and whether pipelines permit resampling or verifier‑guided regeneration [3,4]. Hybrid approaches that combine formal fault localization or symbolic verification with generative repair operators show promise for configuration and program repair but exhibit variable success across fault classes and benchmarks [9,10]. Complementary literature on hallucination detection and deterministic safety nets (entropy‑based detectors, retrieval augmentation, self‑reflection) addresses related detection and mitigation challenges but often outside full NetOps production settings [11,12]. Our study positions itself within these threads by isolating the bounded, post‑hoc verifier/repair effect from resampling benefits through shared_initial conditioning.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered the confirmatory design (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) and fixed the primary estimand: the absolute paired difference in the proportion of unflagged verifier passes (guarded − baseline) on N = 300 paired intents after applying prespecified inclusion/exclusion rules. The preregistration (archived) specified a paired design, the analysis executor, inclusion/exclusion rules, contamination controls, and planned sensitivity analyses. The optional calibration pilot described in the preregistration was not executed; consequently no post‑preregistration power recalculation was performed. We report this omission early in Methods because it materially affects interpretability of inferential sensitivity.

Task generation and stratification. The task suite is a deterministic synthetic topology and intent generator stratified into three difficulty levels (low/medium/high) to ensure balanced sampling (100 pairs per stratum). Each task manifest encodes the natural‑language intent, initial and expected final device states, sequencing constraints (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields), preserve‑state invariants, protected interfaces, and difficulty metadata used for stratum assignment. Representative difficulty patterns include "shutdown_configure_restore" (medium) and "paired_link_atomic_mtu_change" (hard).

Shared_initial protocol and model configuration. To bound the estimand to deterministic validator/repair rescue we used a shared_initial protocol: for each pair we produced exactly one LLM candidate and reused it verbatim for both conditions. The declared generator was gpt-5-mini (requested_model = "gpt-5-mini"); model configuration constrained output length and reasoning effort so that generation variance across conditions is eliminated. This design isolates the post‑generation deterministic effect of validation and bounded automated repair from any benefit due to independent additional model draws.

Validator, scoring rule, and repair operator. Semantic evaluation used a deterministic validator implementing a full_intent_constraint_validation rule set that checks sequencing invariants, required command counts, preservation of unspecified state, topology reachability invariants encoded by the synthetic suite, and protected‑interface constraints. Scoring is binary: an unflagged candidate counts as a pass. The guarded pipeline permitted at most one automated repair attempt per pair; the repair operator is a constrained, localized edit routine limited to sequencing and insertion edits (for example, inserting a missing 'admin down' before changing VLAN/MTU). Repairs are applied only when the validator flags the shared_initial candidate and are re‑validated deterministically. Repair candidates that remain flagged after the permitted edit count count as failures for the guarded condition in the primary analysis.

Contamination controls and missingness rules. The preregistration included negative controls and deterministic contamination checks (invariant tests and intentionally broken control tasks). A pair would be excluded from the confirmatory analysis only if both pipeline calls failed due to provider/infrastructure outage; if only one call failed the pair would be retained per the executor's complete_pair_primary rule with prespecified sensitivity analyses treating single failures as failures. All provider and execution events were logged by instrumentation for reconciliation.
sections.results:
Execution integrity. The registered adapter completed the confirmatory run producing 300 paired observations under the shared_initial protocol. Provider audit recorded 301 hosted model calls (300 shared_initial + 1 repair). No dual‑call provider/infrastructure outages occurred and no pairs were excluded. Deterministic reconciliation checks passed.

Primary confirmatory outcomes. Binary scoring produced baseline_success_count = 299 and guarded_success_count = 300 (baseline rate = 0.996667; guarded = 1.0). The paired contingency counts are n11 = 299, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test (operating on discordant counts n10 and n01) returned p = 1.0. The absolute paired improvement (guarded − baseline) equals 0.0033333. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval (bootstrap_seed = 1729; B = 10000) is [0.00, 0.01]. Because total discordance m = n10 + n01 = 1 is minimal, exact inference has limited sensitivity; the bootstrap CI bounds the plausible absolute improvement to at most one percentage point under the registered estimand and suite.

Per‑stratum diagnostics. Stratified tallies show: low difficulty baseline = 100/100 and guarded = 100/100; medium baseline = 100/100 and guarded = 100/100; high baseline = 99/100 and guarded = 100/100. The single discordant pairing is concentrated in the high difficulty stratum, confirming that observed rescue occurred on a hard sequencing pattern.

Repair diagnostic and episode trace. The solitary discordant pair invoked the permitted automated repair. Validator traces attribute the initial failure to a sequencing omission (a missing 'admin down' prior to a VLAN/MTU change). The constrained automated edit inserted the missing sequencing command, after which the validator reported valid == true. Thus the single repair produced a deterministic rescue under the bounded edit operator and budget. The empirical repair count for the run was one, so the guarded pipeline incurred minimal extra model‑call cost.

Contamination and missingness. Preplanned contamination checks and negative controls produced no unexpected pass behavior; missingness summary reports no failed or unscorable episodes and no excluded pairs under preregistered rules.

Operational cost footprint. The guarded pipeline used one additional model/repair stage call across 300 pairs (301 model calls total), quantifying a low marginal model‑call cost for the observed deterministic rescue in this run.
sections.discussion:
Estimand conditioning and operational relevance. The shared_initial estimand corresponds to operational policies that restrict model calls (cost, latency, governance). Under those policies the guarded pipeline measures only deterministic validation and bounded repair applied to the identical candidate; it does not capture benefits obtainable by resampling or interactive verifier‑guided generation. Evaluations intending to measure those wider benefits must alter the estimand to permit additional model calls or interactive steering.

Ceiling effects and power. Baseline single‑shot performance was near ceiling (299/300) on this synthetic suite. Because the preregistration's optional pilot for discordance estimation was not executed, the run encountered minimal discordance (m = 1) and limited inferential sensitivity for small absolute improvements. This outcome shows the practical value of small calibration pilots when generator performance might approach ceiling on the chosen task distribution.

Validator coverage and failure‑mode dependence. The observed failure mode was sequencing omission; reachability or ACL violations were not observed at scale on the synthetic suite. The guarded pipeline's marginal value therefore depends on the deployment distribution of failure modes and on validator expressiveness. Richer validators that detect complex reachability or policy semantics are likely to increase observed rescue rates; conversely, if operator policy forbids automated edits, guarded pipelines are limited to detection and human escalation.

Repair budget tradeoffs. We intentionally constrained repair to a single localized edit to quantify bounded deterministic rescue. Iterative repair, richer edit operators, or verifier‑guided regeneration would address a different estimand and likely increase rescue opportunities at the cost of additional model calls and governance considerations. Organizations must balance permitted repair complexity, model‑call budgets, and human‑in‑the‑loop policies in CI/CD workflows.

Reproducibility and artifact availability. We archive the preregistration, task manifests, validator traces, repair transcript, and analysis inputs to permit deterministic replay of the registered executor and to support targeted follow‑up studies that vary estimand conditioning, model strength, task distributions, or repair budgets.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired design that conditions on a single LLM draw per intent, adding a deterministic validator plus at most one constrained automated repair produced one deterministic rescue among 300 paired intents (baseline 299/300, guarded 300/300). The absolute paired improvement equals 0.00333 (exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI [0.00, 0.01]). Under the synthetic suite and bounded repair operator used here, baseline single‑shot generation was near ceiling, limiting observable deterministic rescue. These results quantify a conservative, operationally meaningful bound on deterministic verifier/repair rescue under tight model‑call budgets; broader workflows that permit resampling or iterative repair require different estimand definitions and empirical evaluation. We release archived artifacts to support reproducible follow‑up studies and policy‑aligned pipeline design.

limitations: Synthetic benchmark: tasks and topologies were generated deterministically; real‑world heterogeneity may expose different failure modes and increase verifier marginal utility.
Single model and validator: only gpt-5-mini and the declared deterministic validator were evaluated; results may not generalize to other LLMs, validator designs, or richer check sets.
Ceiling effect: baseline single‑shot performance was near 100% (299/300) on this suite, producing minimal discordance and limiting power to detect small absolute improvements.
Pilot omission: the preregistered optional pilot for discordance estimation and power calibration was not run; this reduces sensitivity for detecting small effects in the confirmatory run.

Estimand conditioning: the shared_initial protocol conditions on a single LLM candidate and therefore does not measure verifier benefit obtainable via resampling or iterative verifier‑guided generation.

Repair budget: the guarded condition permitted at most one constrained automated repair; richer or iterative repair strategies may yield different outcomes and require evaluation under a different estimand.
